DetectionMode.blurb: OKAO face-detector operating mode enum (default Movie). Movie is the live-video tracker with multi-frame search/lost/steadiness settings. Still is a single-image detector (no movie tracker). Other listed modes (Default, Whole, Partition 3, Gradual) are in the OKAO enum string but Init only accepts Movie or Still — anything else logs UnknownDetectionMode and fails init.
DetectionMode.detail: Registered as CONSOLE_VAR_ENUM under Vision.FaceDetectorCommon. Applied only inside FaceTracker::Impl::Init when creating the OKAO detection handle (DETECTION_MODE_MOVIE vs DETECTION_MODE_STILL). Movie path also applies SearchCycle, Lost, Steadiness, TrackingSwap, DelayCount, Accuracy, Angle/Pose extension, DirectionMask, and tracking edge masks. Changing this at runtime does nothing until ReinitDetector is pulsed true so Deinit+Init run again. Face-eval host tools force Still for offline images.
DetectionMode.howTo: 1) Set DetectionMode (Movie for on-robot video, Still for single-frame tests). 2) Set ReinitDetector true once so the tracker rebuilds. 3) Confirm face tracking still works.
DetectionMode.statusNote: Read only at face-tracker Init. Runtime changes need ReinitDetector. Init implements only Movie and Still; other enum labels fail Init.

DistanceFromCameraThresholdSq_mm.blurb: Maximum squared distance (mm²) from the camera to a tracked face for “making eye contact” to be allowed. Default 700×700 (= 490000 → face within about 0.7 m). Faces farther away fail the secondary eye-contact constraints even if gaze looks centered.
DistanceFromCameraThresholdSq_mm.detail: EyeContact::SecondaryConstraints requires head pose translation LengthSq() < this threshold, plus head pitch/yaw in cone and blink-amount checks. Used by FaceWorld::IsMakingEyeContact, conditionEyeContact, face selection, track-face, and gaze-react behaviors. Larger values allow eye-contact at greater range; smaller values require the person to be closer.

EnableExtraIlluminationDetectorDebug.blurb: When true, logs extra DEBUG lines from the illumination detector: feature-buffer fill progress, histogram percentile feature vectors, and classifier probability. Off by default. Does not change Illuminated/Darkened decisions — logging only.
EnableExtraIlluminationDetectorDebug.detail: IlluminationDetector runs under VisionMode::Illumination when feature ReactToIllumination is on. It builds a window of image-brightness percentiles and classifies with a linear model from resources. Extra debug is intentionally spammy (comment in source). Pair with Illumination mode / feature gate when tuning thresholds in vision_config IlluminationDetector block.

paths.notes: ClassifierConfigPath and IlluminatedMinProbability / DarkenedMaxProbability live under IlluminationDetector in vision_config.

FakeCatDetectionProbability.blurb: Probability (0–1, default 0) that, after a neural-net run registered to Pets mode, the vision system injects a full-frame fake Cat salient point. For testing pet behaviors when real cat detection is missing or unreliable.
FakeCatDetectionProbability.detail: Only under ANKI_DEV_CHEATS. AddFakeDetections runs after neural-net results; for each mode in the net’s mode set, if Pets is present and a uniform random draw is below this value, appends SalientPointType::Cat covering the whole image. Independent of FakeDogDetectionProbability (both can fire on the same Pets frame). Zero leaves real detections alone.
FakeCatDetectionProbability.howTo: 1) Ensure Pets / neural nets are scheduled. 2) Set this > 0 (e.g. 1.0 for always). 3) Confirm Cat salient points / pet behaviors. Reset to 0 when done.
FakeCatDetectionProbability.statusNote: Only compiled/used when ANKI_DEV_CHEATS is enabled; default 0 means no fakes.

FakeDogDetectionProbability.blurb: Probability (0–1, default 0) of injecting a full-frame fake Dog salient point after a Pets-mode neural-net result. Same dev-cheat path as FakeCatDetectionProbability.
FakeDogDetectionProbability.detail: AddFakeDetections under ANKI_DEV_CHEATS; independent RNG check from cat fakes on the same Pets mode. Used to exercise dog-related AI without a working pet model.

FakeHandDetectionProbability.blurb: Probability (0–1, default 0) of injecting a full-frame fake Hand salient point after a neural-net result registered to Hands mode. For testing hand-reaction behaviors without a reliable hand model.
FakeHandDetectionProbability.detail: Same ANKI_DEV_CHEATS AddFakeDetections path as pet fakes, but keyed on VisionMode::Hands and SalientPointType::Hand.

Gain.blurb: Factory playpen camera gain (default 1.0). When the playpen test behavior activates, it builds fixed CameraParams from Exposure_ms and this Gain (also used for the three white-balance gain channels) and calls SetAndDisableCameraControl so auto-exposure and white balance stop updating.
Gain.detail: WRAP_EXTERN_CONSOLE_VAR of PlaypenConfig::kGain under category Playpen — not the live AutoExp gain floor. Only relevant during factory playpen camera calibration / test sequences. Normal freeplay AE uses CameraParamsController and MIN_CAMERA_GAIN/MAX_CAMERA_GAIN constants, not this var.
Gain.howTo: Only needed when running playpen factory tests. Set before starting playpen; activation snapshots params into SetAndDisableCameraControl.
Gain.statusNote: Playpen/factory only. Does not change freeplay auto-exposure gain.

GetEnrollmentTimeFromImageTimestamp.blurb: When true, face enrollment records use the camera image timestamp as enrollment/update time instead of wall-clock system time. Default false. Mainly for offline/unit tests that process image files faster than real time.
GetEnrollmentTimeFromImageTimestamp.detail: FaceRecognizer_okao uses this when RegisterNewUser and UpdateExistingAlbumEntry build EnrolledFaceEntry::Time. True → Time(milliseconds(image timestamp)); false → system_clock::now(). Host tools (recognizeFaces) and face-recognition tests force true. Production robots should leave false so enrollment ages match real calendar time.

LinearizeForAutoExposure.blurb: When true, auto-exposure converts pixel brightness through the camera linearization LUT (undo gamma) before filling the brightness histogram. Default false. Intended to make exposure math more accurate; often left off as “not super necessary.”
LinearizeForAutoExposure.detail: CameraParamsController::ComputeExposureAdjustment installs linearizeFcn from _linearizationLUT when this is on. Used on grayscale AE path histogram fill. RGB combined AE/WB path comments still TODO linearization for channel sums. Pair with AutoExp; gamma table must be set elsewhere for LUT to be meaningful.

MeteringHoldTime_ms.blurb: After the vision system last used detection boxes (markers, faces, etc.) to drive auto-exposure metering, it freezes AE updates for this many milliseconds (default 2000) once those boxes disappear. Prevents exposure from jumping the moment a face or cube leaves frame.
MeteringHoldTime_ms.detail: In UpdateCameraParams, if MeterFromDetections is on and _meteringRegions is empty, but a prior metering timestamp exists and current image time is still within lastMetering + hold, the function returns early without recomputing exposure. While hold is active you may see log HoldingExposureAfterRecentMeteredRegions. Only matters when AutoExp (and/or WhiteBalance) is running and metering-from-detections is enabled in vision config.

MinCameraGain.blurb: Appears under Vision.PreProcessing as a float defaulting to 0.1, but the value is never read. Real minimum camera gain for AE and APIs is the compile-time constant MIN_CAMERA_GAIN (0.25 on this tree, bandaid for VIC-6653).
MinCameraGain.detail: CONSOLE_VAR kMinCameraGain is registered in visionComponent.cpp only. VisionSystem::GetMinCameraGain returns MIN_CAMERA_GAIN; CameraParamsController uses the min/max passed at construction from those constants. Changing this console id does nothing to live AE or SDK CameraConfigResponse.
MinCameraGain.evidence: engine/components/visionComponent.cpp:85 (register only); engine/vision/visionSystem.h:186; engine/vision/visionSystem.cpp:152-156; robot/include/anki/cozmo/shared/cozmoConfig.h:186-188; rg shows no other kMinCameraGain readers
MinCameraGain.statusNote: Registered but unused. Runtime floor is MIN_CAMERA_GAIN (0.25f), not this console var.

MinDetectionConfidence.blurb: Minimum OKAO face-detection confidence (default 500, typical OKAO scale ~0–1000) required before a tracked face is considered enrollable for face recognition. Does not gate ordinary face tracking — only enrollment eligibility.
MinDetectionConfidence.detail: FaceTracker::Impl::IsEnrollable requires detectionInfo.nConfidence > this value, plus frontal pose, IsFacingCamera, and minimum inter-eye distance. Comment notes that in default tracking accuracy, OKAO may report a fixed track confidence equal to the detection threshold, so this knob may have little effect unless high-accuracy tracking is used. Category Vision.FaceTracker (FaceEnrollParams).

OverExposedAdjustmentFraction.blurb: When the brightness histogram’s top bin (fully saturated pixels) exceeds MaxFractionOverexposed, AE multiplies exposure by this fraction (default 0.5, range 0–1) instead of the normal target/percentile ratio — a hard step-down for badly blown-out frames.
OverExposedAdjustmentFraction.detail: CameraParamsController::ComputeAdjustmentFraction special case. Lower values darken faster when washed out; 1.0 would not reduce on overexposure via this path. Works with AutoExp whenever the histogram is rebuilt for exposure.

OverExposedThreshold.blurb: RGB channel value above which a pixel is treated as over-exposed (strictly greater than this, default 240 on 0–255). Over/under-exposed pixels are skipped when summing channels for gray-world white balance. Set both this and UnderExposedThreshold to 0 to treat every pixel as well-exposed.
OverExposedThreshold.detail: IsWellExposed requires each of R,G,B in [UnderExposedThreshold, OverExposedThreshold]. Used in ComputeWhiteBalanceAdjustment and the combined RGB AE+WB path. Does not by itself trigger the OverExposedAdjustmentFraction histogram special case (that uses the top hist bin vs MaxFractionOverexposed).

PostClaheSmooth.blurb: Smoothing applied after CLAHE contrast enhancement used for marker detection. Default −3: box filter of size 3. 0 = no smooth. Positive = Gaussian sigma (kernel ~3×sigma, forced odd). Negative = box-filter size = −value.
PostClaheSmooth.detail: Runs only when ApplyCLAHE actually produces a CLAHE image (_currentUseCLAHE). Affects the image fed to DetectMarkers when UseCLAHE_u8 is On/Both/Alternating/WhenDark (not Off). Playpen calibration temporarily forces UseCLAHE_u8 off then restores WhenDark (4).

ReinitDetector.blurb: One-shot: set true to tear down and re-create the OKAO face detector on the next face-tracker Update, applying current FaceDetectorCommon console params (DetectionMode, sizes, thresholds, movie params, etc.). Automatically clears back to false after reinit.
ReinitDetector.detail: Only present when REMOTE_CONSOLE_ENABLED. FaceTracker::Impl::Update checks the flag, Deinit(), Init(), then sets the flag false. Use after changing DetectionMode or other init-only OKAO knobs. May briefly interrupt face tracking.
ReinitDetector.howTo: 1) Change face-detector console params as needed. 2) Set ReinitDetector true. 3) Wait one vision faces tick; flag self-clears. 4) Verify faces still track.

RollingShutterCorrectionEnabled.blurb: When true (default), physical robots enable rolling-shutter correction so vision can compensate for motion distortion across camera rows using IMU/pose history. When false, correction is forced off and vision-while-rotating-fast is also disabled.
RollingShutterCorrectionEnabled.detail: Read only inside VisionComponent::SetCameraCalibration: if enabled, ShouldDoRollingShutterCorrection(robot.IsPhysical()); else false + EnableVisionWhileRotatingFast(false). Simulator/non-physical stays off even if the flag is true. Runtime toggle after calibration was set does nothing until calibration is applied again. Correction itself runs in VisionSystem::UpdateRollingShutter via RollingShutterCorrector.
RollingShutterCorrectionEnabled.howTo: Prefer setting before/at camera calibration. To re-apply after boot, force a path that calls SetCameraCalibration again (e.g. recalibrate) after changing the flag.
RollingShutterCorrectionEnabled.statusNote: Only applied when SetCameraCalibration runs, not every frame. False also turns off vision-while-rotating-fast.

SensorAperture.blurb: Not a camera setting. Multiplier that turns a ToF/prox distance reading into a sensor-beam width for the navigation map (default 0.4 ≈ tan of half-cone). Beam width = measurement × SensorAperture; obstacle width is that value clamped by MaxObstacleWidth_mm.
SensorAperture.detail: ProxSensorComponent clear-region / obstacle geometry: wider aperture clears a fatter cone but can create large far obstacles (comments warn about planning failures). Category ProxSensorComponent — unrelated to camera aperture/f-stop.

UnderExposedThreshold.blurb: RGB channel value below which a pixel is treated as under-exposed (strictly less than this, default 15). Together with OverExposedThreshold, filters which pixels contribute to white-balance channel sums. Both thresholds 0 → every pixel counts as well-exposed.
UnderExposedThreshold.detail: IsWellExposed helper in CameraParamsController. Same WB statistics path as OverExposedThreshold. Does not define the “TooDark” image-quality message (that uses separate vision_config percentiles).

UseCLAHE_u8.blurb: Selects how CLAHE (local contrast boost) is used before marker detection. Integer 0–4 mapping MarkerDetectionCLAHE: 0 Off, 1 On (CLAHE only), 2 Both (original then CLAHE), 3 Alternating frames, 4 WhenDark (default — CLAHE only if image mean is below ClaheWhenDarkThreshold). Improves reading fiducials in uneven lighting at CPU cost.
UseCLAHE_u8.detail: Cast to MarkerDetectionCLAHE each vision Update; ApplyCLAHE may leave claheImage empty when Off or WhenDark-and-bright. DetectMarkers chooses gray vs CLAHE pointers from the same mode. Playpen camera calibration sets 0 while capturing the calib image, then restores 4. Not used for face detection. Related knobs: ClaheClipLimit, ClaheTileSize, ClaheWhenDarkThreshold, PostClaheSmooth.
UseCLAHE_u8.howTo: 0 for raw markers / calib; 4 for product-like dark scenes; 2 if you want max chance at cost of two detector passes.

UseCenterWeightedMetering.blurb: When true (default) and no explicit metering weight mask from detections, auto-exposure weights the green-channel histogram toward the image center (L1 falloff from mid-frame). When false, every subsampled pixel counts equally.
UseCenterWeightedMetering.detail: In ComputeExposureAndWhiteBalance: if GetMeteringWeightMask already has detection weights, those win; else if this flag, center weights; else uniform. Only affects RGB AE/WB combined path histogram. Detection-based metering (faces/markers) bypasses center weighting via the weight mask.

WhiteBalance.blurb: Force-enables VisionMode::WhiteBalance so the engine continuously adjusts camera red/blue gains toward gray-world balance from well-exposed pixels. Default product schedule also runs WhiteBalance about every 5th frame from vision_config. When off (and nothing subscribed it), WB gains stay at their last values.
WhiteBalance.detail: SetupVisionModeConsoleVars registers every VisionMode name as a bool under Vision.General.VisionModes; toggling true DevOnly-subscribes and EnableMode. UpdateCameraParams sets WhiteBalanceMode::GrayWorld when the mode is on, computing adjR/adjB so channel averages match green (skipping under/over-exposed pixels). Applied to the camera via CameraService::CameraSetWhiteBalanceParameters when the mode was processed. Playpen/manual SetAndDisableCameraControl turns WB off and forces fixed gains. Sibling of AutoExp; both can run in the same UpdateCameraParams call.
